Fixes #102236. A startup overflow catch-up slot could be persisted to SQLite while its protection marker existed only in memory. Restarting again before that slot fired let maintenance advance the job to its next natural cron slot, silently losing the deferred run.

## Summary

- add experimental `claws export <agent-id> --out <new-directory>`
- project one installed agent into the grouped portable Claw schema
- copy ledger-managed workspace files and safe workspace-relative avatars into package sidecars

target.title: Add plan-first Claw status and remove
target.body:
## Summary

- add experimental `claws status [claw-or-agent]` for agent, workspace-file, partial-state, and package-reference visibility
- add plan-first `claws remove <claw-or-agent> --dry-run --json` with separate `--yes` consent
- reuse canonical agent deletion and identity-safe managed-file cleanup
- uninstall a final, unchanged Claw-installed plugin or skill through its existing owner lifecycle
- retain pre-existing, shared, pending, modified, missing, or ambiguous artifacts and report why

## Scope

This is the status/remove slice for the grouped one-Claw/one-agent contract. Package names resolve an install only when unambiguous; final agent ids always work and disambiguate repeated adds.

Remove revalidates the agent digest, managed files, and package decisions before mutation. Agent drift and unsafe workspace paths block the plan. Missing files are already removed, locally modified files are retained, and unchanged files are moved to nonce staging paths before final digest validation and deletion.

Package removal is ownership-aware. A completed `claw-installed` skill is removed only from its owning agent workspace after strict ClawHub origin, lock, version, and `SKILL.md` digest validation. A plugin is removed only when no other Claw references its ClawHub package and its installed identity/version still match; execution delegates to the canonical plugin uninstall command. When the original installing Claw is removed while another Claw still references a global plugin, ownership transfers to a surviving reference so the eventual final removal remains correct. Package-plan changes after dry-run fail revalidation instead of escalating consent.

If package or file cleanup fails after the agent config commit, the root ledger remains partial and subordinate references stay available for status/doctor recovery. All commands remain gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`, and JSON contracts remain experimental.

target.title: fix(gateway): don't retire parent Codex binding when creating a detached dashboard child
target.body:
Fixes #106778

## What Problem This Solves

Creating a dashboard child from an active Codex-backed channel session (Control UI → new dashboard chat — an ordinary child creation, not a fork) succeeds but **retires the parent session's Codex binding**, even though the parent remains the channel's current session. The next inbound parent turn then fails permanently with `Codex binding generation was retired`, recoverable only by manual SQLite surgery.

Root-cause chain (all on current `main`):
1. `createGatewaySession` emits a terminal `session_end(reason:"new")` on the **parent** for any parent-linked child when `emitCommandHooks === true` — `src/gateway/session-create-service.ts`.
2. The Codex extension treats `"new"` as terminal (`ENDED_SESSION_REASONS`) and its `session_end` handler calls `bindingStore.retireSessionGeneration()` — `extensions/codex/index.ts:48,274`.
3. The next lease attempt observes the retired generation and throws `Codex binding generation was retired`.

A detached dashboard child (its own `agent:<id>:dashboard:*` key) runs **in parallel** — it does not replace the parent as the channel's current session, so emitting a terminal `session_end` on the parent is wrong.

## Approach

The parent rolls over — terminal `session_end` on the parent, `session_start` on the child — only when the child **succeeds** it. That disposition cannot be inferred from the child's key shape: the server keeps no current-session pointer, so a key namespace cannot prove succession (the earlier `startsWith("dashboard:")` gate was a heuristic). The caller declares it explicitly via a new optional `succeedsParent` flag on `sessions.create`; the gate reads the flag:

```ts
const childSucceedsParent = params.fork !== true && params.succeedsParent === true;
```

The namespace invariant is enforced by a **loud boundary validation** rather than silent inference: `succeedsParent` requires an explicit non-dashboard successor key and conflicts with `fork`; a keyless/minted or dashboard-namespaced child (auto-managed, detached) is rejected with `INVALID_REQUEST`. A mis-declared succession therefore fails loudly instead of silently retiring a still-active parent's binding.

- **Only TUI `/new`** (an explicit `tui-*` successor) declares `succeedsParent: true` — it still emits the parent `session_end` + child `session_start`.
- **Every other create path** — minted dashboard child (webchat "new chat"), fork, catalog/work child — is parallel by default and unchanged: no parent `session_end`, child `session_start` fires.

Closes #107255

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users opening an external plugin Control UI tab would see the embedded panel fail with `401 Unauthorized` when the plugin route uses Gateway auth and the Gateway is running in token/password auth mode.

## Why This Change Was Made

External plugin tab descriptors already advertise gateway-local `path` values, and the Control UI should keep rendering those tabs as ordinary sandboxed iframes. This change issues short-lived, signed, HttpOnly plugin-tab cookies after authenticated Control UI read auth, then accepts those cookies only inside the plugin HTTP route auth stage.

The cookie handoff is now bounded in two ways:

- Browser cookie `Path` is scoped to each advertised external plugin tab path.
- The signed payload carries the same route path and the current shared Gateway auth generation, so sibling plugin routes and stale credentials are rejected before runtime scopes are derived.

Direct unauthenticated plugin route requests still return `401`, Gateway credentials are not placed in iframe URLs, and external tab rendering stays a normal `iframe src` load.

## User Impact

Operators can open external plugin Control UI tabs whose HTTP routes are protected with `auth: "gateway"` instead of making those routes public, switching to plugin-managed auth, or putting Gateway credentials in iframe URLs.

## Evidence

## What Problem This Solves

Outbound Synology Chat responses previously buffered response bodies without a byte cap, risking Gateway OOM within the request timeout. Inbound webhooks were already bounded.

## Changes

- **Chatbot POST (status-only):** success follows HTTP status; unused body is destroyed/discarded without buffering so a large 200 body cannot flip a successful send into a false failure or unbounded memory growth.
- **user_list:** keep bounded body reads (1 MiB) with cache fallback on overflow.

**CI hang fix (f9ad8e376cf9):** prior tip had 23/24 pass; overflow-only test timed out 120s because `res.destroy()` without error often skips `end`/`error`. Now settle (`finish` + warn) **before** destroy; overflow fixture uses one oversized Buffer.



**CI root-cause fix (9f3ca4d8b96e):** `readRequestBodyWithLimit` left `user_list` resolves empty under the existing PassThrough mocks. Switched to sync bounded Buffer accumulation (UTF-8 safe + 1 MiB overflow → cache), keeping main `res.resume()` and #108019 stream UTF-8 tests.


**CI fix (5bb45cfef281):** user_list tests use real timers + deferred mock body emit so `readRequestBodyWithLimit` can settle; body-limit errors (including destroy race) map to overflow/cache fallback.


### Conflict resolution vs #108019 (43a86a604a77)

Rebased onto current `main` `4e756adaaf6a` after #108019 (`65d55d046baa`).

| Kept (this PR) | Left to main (#108019) |
|---|---|
| Bounded `user_list` via `readRequestBodyWithLimit` (1 MiB) | Native UTF-8 via Buffer concat (no string `+=`) |
| Overflow → warn + cache/empty fallback | POST unused body: `res.resume()` |
| Test: overflow cap via `resolveLegacyWebhookNameToChatUserId` | Real PassThrough stream UTF-8 split nickname test |

Removed duplicate POST destroy/drain fork and manual `setEncoding("utf8")` + unbounded string accumulation. No new public export of `fetchChatUsers`.

First submitted: July 6, 2026, 10:00 PM (US Eastern Time) / 02:00 UTC.
Last body edit: July 15, 2026, 3:56 AM (US Eastern Time) / 07:56 UTC.
Latest head commit: July 15, 2026, 3:47 AM (US Eastern Time) / 07:47 UTC.
<!-- submission-timestamps:end -->

Closes #101204

## What Problem This Solves

A configured but temporarily missing built-in TTS API-key SecretRef currently aborts Gateway startup and takes unrelated chat, auth, tools, channels, and plugins offline even though only speech synthesis needs that credential. This PR keeps the first activating startup available while preserving strict failure for every non-activating, reload, restart-check, config-write, malformed-ref, policy, provider, contract, mismatch, and invalid-value path.

## Summary

A missing built-in TTS provider API-key SecretRef no longer aborts an otherwise healthy Gateway during the first activating startup. The affected TTS provider remains unconfigured, startup emits a structured warning, and unrelated chat, auth, tools, channels, and plugins continue to start.

The exception is deliberately narrow. It requires all of the following:

- the lifecycle reason is `startup`;
- the operation will activate the prepared snapshot (`activate === true`);
- no active secrets runtime snapshot exists;
- the assignment is a built-in TTS provider API key explicitly marked optional; and
- resolution failed with the matching missing-value error for that exact ref.

Non-activating startup preparation, restart checks, reloads, config-write preflight, malformed refs, policy/security failures, provider failures, contract failures, mismatched errors, and invalid resolved value shapes remain fail-closed.

## Breaking changes

There is no config-shape, RPC, persistence, package, or dependency change. Failure timing changes for one credential class: a missing built-in TTS API-key SecretRef is reported as a startup warning and fails locally when that TTS provider is used, rather than aborting the entire first activating Gateway startup.

## Why / user impact

Built-in TTS is an optional capability, but SecretRef activation previously treated its API keys as credentials required by the whole Gateway. Operators may now keep an optional ElevenLabs or other built-in TTS SecretRef configured while its value is temporarily absent. The provider remains unavailable until the ref resolves, while unrelated Gateway capabilities stay online.

The stricter sibling paths are unchanged: reload, restart-check, non-activating startup preparation, and config-write preflight reject the unresolved ref and preserve the last-known-good runtime/config.

## Implementation

- `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts` owns the lifecycle gate. Optional missing-value degradation is enabled only for `reason === "startup"`, `activate === true`, and an absent active runtime snapshot.
- The lifecycle gate is layered onto the current mainline `resolveGatewayStartupSecretProjection` contract. `sourceConfig` remains the recoverable full source, while an `assignmentConfig` may suppress unsafe channel assignments during crash-loop recovery; this PR does not collapse those responsibilities back into one pruned config.
- `src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.ts` marks only built-in TTS provider API-key assignments as optional at startup.
- `src/secrets/resolve-errors.ts` owns typed provider/ref errors and the exact missing-value classifier; `src/secrets/resolve.ts` assigns those codes at env/file/exec and provider-contract boundaries.
- `src/secrets/runtime-optional-assignments.ts` owns required/optional partitioning, independent optional resolution, warning emission, and redaction registration.
- `src/secrets/runtime-prepare.runtime.ts` exports that helper through the existing lazy startup facade, so the Gateway hot path does not statically load the full resolver.
- `src/secrets/runtime.ts` delegates assignment resolution once and remains focused on snapshot preparation/activation.
- `src/secrets/runtime-shared.ts` carries optional-assignment metadata while retaining existing resolved-value shape validation.

## Code-path analysis

- Runtime entry: `src/gateway/server-startup-config.ts` prepares secrets before Gateway startup activation.
- Lifecycle owner: `createRuntimeSecretsActivator` decides whether preparation is activating and whether a prior runtime snapshot exists.
- Mainline projection boundary: `src/gateway/server-startup-secret-surfaces.ts` separates recoverable source config from the assignment projection used during crash-loop recovery.
- Snapshot owner: `src/secrets/runtime.ts` prepares and activates the runtime snapshot.
- Optional-assignment owner: `src/secrets/runtime-optional-assignments.ts` resolves optional refs independently without weakening the required batch.
- Collector/caller: `src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors.ts` routes core/channel/plugin surfaces; `src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.ts` collects top-level, agent, and channel voice TTS API keys.
- Resolver/callee: `src/secrets/resolve.ts` resolves env/file/exec refs; `src/secrets/resolve-errors.ts` distinguishes absence from policy, validation, provider, and contract failures.
- Sibling invariant: Gateway auth, model/provider, plugin, channel-token, auth-store, and all other required assignments remain fail-closed.
- Localized runtime failure: `src/gateway/server-methods/tts.ts` returns the normal provider-not-configured `UNAVAILABLE` path when the degraded provider is selected.
- Adjacent coverage: `src/secrets/resolve.test.ts`, `src/secrets/runtime.test.ts`, `src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts`, `src/secrets/runtime-discord-surface.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-config.secrets.test.ts`, `src/gateway/server-methods/config.shared-auth.test.ts`, and `src/gateway/server-methods/tts.test.ts`.

## Mainline comparison

Rebased onto `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@4f71a2855e538185d16e7b04d3acc7f2f02a3944` (commit time 2026-07-15T07:43:03Z; fetched 2026-07-15T07:47Z).

Recent same-area mainline work was incorporated rather than overwritten:

- `701d02f241` made the Gateway startup secret-assignment projection explicit.
- `1eec68a6a0` preserved safe-mode secret recovery when suppressed channel secrets are unavailable.
- `3616fba951` made hot reload transactional.

The final rebase increment through `4f71a2855e` changed unrelated auto-reply tests, status formatting, signed-merge handling, Codex restricted-turn shell behavior, and Telegram archive fixtures. During the final exact-head proof, official `main` advanced through `1fe3a5f557` with plugin compatibility, terminal quoting, Codex adapter, and Testbox path changes; the GitHub compare contains no changes under this PR's startup lifecycle gate, `src/secrets/`, or TTS docs/tests.

- Head: `snowzlmbot/OpenClaw:fix/optional-tts-secret-startup@9a4986f4c3bafd96c69568794e522060c3e0608c`

Observed automated labels include `gateway`, `docs`, compatibility risk, and security-boundary risk. No contributor-side label mutation was performed. The compatibility and security labels remain appropriate because the PR deliberately changes startup behavior for one credential class inside the shared secrets runtime.

- [Exact-head focused tests and live Gateway/RPC proof](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29398667816) — passed on evidence head `5c712d5c05475d5984ce73b36309202d2c367896`, whose direct parent is code head `9a4986f4c3bafd96c69568794e522060c3e0608c`. The final rebase only advanced across unrelated mainline commits; stable patch-id for the complete PR diff remained `eec8e924514251d650ca5a89d501be1517bcd1b7`.
- Exact-current-head PR gates passed for CodeQL Critical Quality, OpenGrep PR diff, Workflow Sanity, Security Sensitive Guard, Dependency Guard, and the upstream Real behavior proof dispatcher. The current full CI and CodeQL runs remain linked in the PR check rollup.

## Evidence source map

[Evidence workflow run](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29398667816)

- Purpose: focused resolver/runtime/TTS collector/Discord voice/Gateway startup/TTS handler regression suite plus live Gateway/RPC behavior.

- Environment: GitHub-hosted Linux runner, Node.js 24.
- Artifact: focused-test and live-proof text logs uploaded by the run.
- PR-only workflow, harness, and logs remain on the dedicated evidence branch and are absent from the code diff.

## Sanitized logs

```text

Tests       33 passed (33)
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests       57 passed (57)
Gateway started with missing optional ELEVENLABS_API_KEY SecretRef.
[SECRETS_REF_UNAVAILABLE_OPTIONAL] messages.tts.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey ... Environment variable "ELEVENLABS_API_KEY" is missing or empty.
TTS conversion failed: elevenlabs: not configured
PASS: missing optional TTS SecretRef degraded startup and localized TTS failure.
```

The proof uses placeholder credential identifiers and redacts generated tokens, temporary paths, and dynamic local addresses.

## Media evidence

This change has no UI or visual state. The relevant behavior is a deterministic startup lifecycle plus RPC path, so the complete Actions execution and uploaded logs provide stronger evidence than a screenshot or video. No timing-dependent user interaction is involved.

## Risk

- Compatibility: operators who relied on whole-Gateway fail-fast for an optional TTS key will now discover that missing value when TTS is used.
- Security boundary: the exception lives in shared secrets startup code, so it is gated by lifecycle state, assignment metadata, exact ref matching, and the typed missing-value classifier.
- Lifecycle regression: non-activating startup preparation, restart-check, reload, active-snapshot startup preparation, and config-write preflight are explicitly covered as strict paths.
- Performance: optional refs are resolved independently; work is bounded by configured built-in TTS provider keys and avoids one missing optional provider masking another valid provider.
- Required credentials, policy denials, invalid refs, provider/contract errors, mismatched refs, and invalid resolved shapes remain fatal and are covered by regression tests.

## Rollback

Revert the two PR commits. No config, database, cache, serialized state, or data migration rollback is required. Existing SecretRefs remain valid; rollback restores universal startup fail-fast behavior for missing built-in TTS provider keys.

## Docs updated

- `docs/gateway/secrets.md`
- `docs/reference/secretref-credential-surface.md`
- `docs/tools/tts.md`

The docs describe the missing-value-only first-activation exception and the normal localized provider-not-configured error.

## Related issue / PR

- Canonical issue: #101204
- Duplicate report: #101205
- Adjacent persona-level SecretRef work: #89607 and #89636 (collection/injection scope, not missing-value startup policy)

## Not tested / limitations

- The live Gateway proof covers a missing env-backed ElevenLabs key.
- Missing file values are covered by optional-runtime tests; missing exec-provider ids are covered by resolver classification tests rather than separate live Gateway runs.
- No real provider API call is attempted because the behavior under test is the absent-credential boundary.
- This PR does not add a persistent `degraded` / `configured_unavailable` state or a new status/doctor/audit projection. It provides the structured startup warning and localized runtime failure; broader observability remains a separate product-scope decision.
- Maintainer product acceptance is still required for the scoped fail-open startup policy.

## Review context addressed

The P1 lifecycle finding is resolved by requiring `activationParams.activate === true` in addition to `reason === "startup"` and no active snapshot. A dedicated regression now proves that non-activating startup preparation with no active snapshot remains fail-closed. Restart-check, reload, active-snapshot preparation, and config-write preflight strictness remain covered.

The previous proof-provenance blocker is also resolved: the final evidence commit's direct parent is the exact PR code head, and the linked run exercises both the focused suite and the live Gateway/RPC path on that parent.

target.title: fix(anthropic): preserve Retry-After header from transport error responses for auto-retry backoff
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103849. When the Anthropic Messages transport receives an HTTP 429 rate-limit error with a `Retry-After` header (e.g. `Retry-After: 30`), the header value is discarded. The error is turned into a plain `Error` carrying only the response body text. Downstream, `AgentSession.prepareRetry` falls back to fixed 2s/4s/8s exponential backoff, so all retries land inside the still-active server cooldown window and the turn fails outright instead of succeeding after the server's actual cooldown.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three coordinated changes, each at its correct ownership boundary:

1. **`createAnthropicMessagesClient`** (`src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts`) — parses the `Retry-After` HTTP header on non-OK responses and attaches `status` (number) and `retryAfterSeconds` (number) to the thrown `Error`.

2. **`extractTransportErrorDetails`** (`src/agents/transport-stream-shared.ts`) — reads `status` and `retryAfterSeconds` from enriched error objects and returns them in `TransportErrorDetails`, which `Object.assign` propagates onto the `AssistantMessage` via `assignTransportErrorDetails`.

3. **`prepareRetry`** (`src/agents/sessions/agent-session.ts`) — when the `AssistantMessage` carries a `retryAfterSeconds` value, uses `Math.max(exponentialDelayMs, retryAfterMs)` instead of purely exponential backoff, so retries wait at least as long as the server requests.

`AssistantMessage` type (`packages/llm-core/src/types.ts`) gains optional `status?: number` and `retryAfterSeconds?: number` fields, consistent with the existing `errorCode`/`errorType`/`errorBody` error metadata pattern.

The existing `parseRetryAfterSeconds` in `provider-transport-fetch.ts` is already correct but only feeds the `x-should-retry` SDK path. A lightweight inline `parseRetryAfterHeaderSeconds` was added closer to the non-SDK client site to keep module dependency boundaries clean.

## User Impact

Users with `anthropic-messages` providers (direct Anthropic API, proxy/third-party gateways returning `Retry-After` headers) now get auto-retry that respects the server's actual cooldown window. When the server sends `Retry-After: 30`, retries wait at least 30 seconds before re-attempting instead of hammering with 2s/4s/8s backoff.

No behavior change for transports that do not attach `retryAfterSeconds` to errors — those continue with the existing exponential backoff. No behavior change for successful (200) responses.

## Evidence

- **TypeScript**: `pnpm tsgo:core` — passes
- **Tests**:
  - `transport-stream-shared.test.ts`: 12/12 ✓ (2 new: `status`/`retryAfterSeconds` extraction from enriched errors, graceful absence on plain errors)
  - `anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`: 108/108 ✓ (1 new: HTTP 429 + `Retry-After: 30` → error carries `status: 429`, `retryAfterSeconds: 30`)
  - `provider-transport-fetch.test.ts`: 94/94 ✓
  - `retry.test.ts`: 21/21 ✓
  - `embedded-agent-runner/helpers.test.ts`: 16/16 ✓
  - `session/settings-manager.test.ts`: 3/3 ✓
  Fixes #103849

## Problem

`sendImageFeishu` and `sendFileFeishu` do a bare `client.im.message.reply()` with no withdrawn/not-found fallback. When the reply target message is deleted or recalled, Feishu returns code 230011 or 231003, and the image/file message is silently dropped. Text and card replies already survive this via `sendReplyOrFallbackDirect`.

Fixes #98311

## Changes

- Export `isWithdrawnReplyError` and `shouldFallbackFromReplyTarget` from `send.ts`
- `sendImageFeishu`: catch withdrawn reply errors and fall back to top-level `im.message.create`
- `sendFileFeishu`: same try/catch + fallback for file/audio/video replies
- Thread replies (`replyInThread`) never fall back — matching the existing thread safety contract in `sendReplyOrFallbackDirect`

## Testing

- TypeScript compilation passes (`tsc --noEmit`)
- Reuses the same detection logic already covered by `send.reply-fallback.test.ts`

target.title: fix(gateway): evict stale ACP runtime handle on cancel/close timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`/reset` on an ACP-backed session cannot recover when `cancelSession` or `closeSession` times out, because the early-return path leaves the stale runtime handle in the manager cache — the next message reuses the same poisoned backend process.
- Problem: `closeAcpRuntimeForSession` returns an `UNAVAILABLE` error on cancel/close timeout without evicting the cached runtime handle, so the next `ensureSession` finds and reuses the stale handle and its corrupted session state. The only recovery is a full gateway restart.
- Solution: On cancel or close timeout, evict the stale handle from `ManagerRuntimeHandleCache` immediately and continue to ACP meta reset (`ensureFreshAcpResetState`) so the next message creates a fresh backend process.
- What changed: `src/acp/control-plane/manager.core.ts` (add `evictSessionHandle` — 4 lines), `src/gateway/session-reset-service.ts` (replace `return errorShape` with evict + continue on both cancel and close timeout — +12 lines net)
- What did NOT change: Happy path (successful cancel→close→meta reset); `closeSession` actor-queue semantics; ACPX persisted-session reuse logic; `deferResetState` caller; zombie process lifecycle (already a timeout risk)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #106631
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

(Using "Related to" rather than "Fixes" because the zombie-process lifecycle issue (the timed-out ACP process may never exit) is a pre-existing concern not addressed by this change.)

## Motivation

Users with ACP-backed sessions (Codex, custom model endpoints via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) sometimes encounter stuck cancel/close cleanup when the backend process is hung on an API call. The gateway's 15s cleanup timeout fires, `closeAcpRuntimeForSession` returns `UNAVAILABLE`, and the stale runtime handle stays in `ManagerRuntimeHandleCache`. The next message immediately reuses the same process and its corrupted session state. The `/reset` command fails to recover, and the only workaround is restarting the entire gateway — which disrupts all sessions across all accounts.

This fix ensures that `/reset` always completes (even with partial cleanup) by evicting the stale handle from the cache on timeout, so the next message creates a fresh process.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Stale ACP runtime handle survives cancel/close timeout in `closeAcpRuntimeForSession`, poisoning subsequent sessions and defeating `/reset` recovery.

**Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.3 (nvm), branch `fix/acp-force-discard-timeout-106631`

```
import { AcpSessionManager } from "./src/acp/control-plane/manager.js";
```

- `03-diff-stat.txt` — `+46/-33` across 2 files
- `04-full-diff.txt` — full patch
- `05-timeout-simulation-output.txt` — raw terminal output of Layer 4 (ACP timeout simulation)
- Gateway integration test: `node openclaw.mjs gateway --port 18789` → `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`

**Matrix-style evidence**:

| Scenario | Current main | After fix |
|----------|-------------|-----------|
| Cancel succeeds, close succeeds | `runtimeHandles.clear()`, meta reset | Same (unchanged) |
| Cancel times out | `return errorShape` — handle STALE, meta NOT reset | `evictSessionHandle()`, skip close, meta reset ✅ |
| Cancel succeeds, close times out | `return errorShape` — handle STALE, meta NOT reset | `evictSessionHandle()`, meta reset ✅ |
| Non-existent session | `return undefined` (no-op) | Same (unchanged) |

**Observed result after fix**:
1. Cancel timeout: handle evicted from cache, closeSession skipped (actor queue owned by timed-out cancel), ACP meta reset to "pending" — next message creates fresh session
2. Close timeout: handle evicted from cache, ACP meta reset to "pending" — next message creates fresh session
3. Happy path: unchanged cancel→close→meta reset with handle cleanup
4. All 12 existing `manager.runtime-handles.test.ts` tests continue to pass
5. 28/29 `manager.test.ts` pass (1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this change)

**What was not tested**: Real ACP backend process with a hung 15s cleanup timeout (requires live ACP runtime, not available in local dev) — **covered by simulation**: Layer 4 uses a mock backend with `cancelSession`/`closeSession` that hang forever (exactly like a stuck Codex process) against the real `AcpSessionManager`, confirming that `evictSessionHandle` works correctly and does not block on the hung operations.

**Gateway integration test** (Node 22.22.3): Gateway started successfully on port 18789, health endpoint returns `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}`, no ACP-related errors in startup logs. The fix compiles and runs correctly in the full gateway runtime.

**Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
- ✅ Auth guard: No new paths — pure logic fix inside existing function. No policy/permission/feature flag needed.
- ✅ Enum completeness: Both timeout branches (cancel + close) handled. Happy path unchanged. Non-timeout error paths continue to log and proceed as before.
- ✅ Path coverage: All 4 callers of `closeAcpRuntimeForSession` covered — parent session (L727), mutation session (L1061), children (L670) return early for timeout too; children's error is logged best-effort.
- ✅ Cleanup symmetry: `evictSessionHandle()` clears the cached entry synchronously. No state leak — the evicted handle's `runtime.close()` was already signaled by the timed-out cancel/close call. ACP meta reset restores fresh state. Fire-and-forget close is not used (would risk re-hanging — see Best-fix Verdict).

## Root Cause

`closeAcpRuntimeForSession` (introduced in `392a02a3960`, PR #104668) races `cancelSession` and `closeSession` against a 15s timeout. When either times out, the function returns `errorShape(UNAVAILABLE)` immediately without evicting the cached runtime handle. The next `ensureSession` finds the stale handle in `ManagerRuntimeHandleCache` and reuses the same poisoned ACP process, defeating `/reset` recovery.

Carried forward by: the original session-reset-service refactor that extracted ACP cleanup into a dedicated function with the timeout guard but without cleanup-on-timeout.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with ACP-backed sessions (Codex, custom `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`) whose `/reset` previously required a full gateway restart after a stuck cancel/close can now recover with `/reset` directly. No other user-visible changes.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — timeout path already returned an error; this change makes it succeed instead. Happy path unchanged.
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — evicting the cached handle on timeout is the minimal correct guard. The stale handle is the only path by which a poisoned session survives `/reset`, so removing it from the cache alongside meta reset is sufficient.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the function's structure is sound; this adds the missing cleanup-on-timeout path.
- **Alternative considered**: fire-and-forget `runtime.close()` on timeout (approach in wuqxuan's closed PR #107374). Rejected because: (1) the timed-out cancel already sent its signal to the same unresponsive runtime, so a second close would also hang; (2) ClawSweeper flagged `merge-risk: 🚨 availability` — fire-and-forget close risks leaving zombie processes; (3) eviction alone is sufficient because the cache entry is what the next `ensureSession` checks. Without the cache entry spawned, a fresh `ensureSession` creates a new backend process regardless of whether the old one eventually responds.
- **Design principle chosen**: Conservative — clear cache only, do not fire-and-forget close.
- **What is solved**: The stale handle — the single path by which a poisoned session survives `/reset`. After eviction the next message always creates a fresh process, restoring `/reset` recovery without a gateway restart.
- **What remains unsolved**: The timed-out ACP process may never exit (zombie resource leak). This is a **pre-existing concern** — the current timeout path already has it, and this fix does not regress on it. A fully clean process-tree reap would require OS-level `SIGTERM→SIGKILL` lifecycle management, which is a separate feature outside the scope of this bug fix.
- **Why this trade-off is optimal**: The alternative (fire-and-forget `runtime.close()`) was considered and rejected because (a) the same unresponsive runtime that hung cancel/close would also hang close, so it solves nothing; (b) it was flagged `merge-risk: 🚨 availability` in the prior PR. Eviction alone is sufficient to restore `/reset` — the user's core problem — with zero new risk.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: iCodeMate <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: The fix was produced in an interactive session analyzing the bug in `closeAcpRuntimeForSession`. The AI suggested adding `evictSessionHandle` to the manager and restructuring the timeout path to continue rather than return early, and the human verified all four callers and both test scenarios.

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: The timed-out cancel or close operation may still be running in the background after the handle is evicted. If the old process eventually completes and tries to update state, there is a theoretical write-write race with the new session.

**Mitigation**: The gateway's ACP manager serializes per-session operations through `withSessionActor`. After eviction, the next `ensureSession` creates a new actor entry. The old actor entry (still held by the timed-out operation) runs to completion independently and is eventually garbage-collected. No shared mutable state is corrupted because each actor has its own cache entry and runtime handle.

**Compatibility impact**: None for the happy path. Users who were previously getting `UNAVAILABLE` on `/reset` after a stuck cancel/close will now get a successful reset (behavior improvement).

target.title: feat(browser): side panel copilot with per-tab agent sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

#100619 gave OpenClaw a way to **drive** your signed-in Chrome: the bundled extension
attaches with `chrome.debugger`, and the OpenClaw tab group is the consent boundary. What it
does not give you is a way to **talk to the agent about the tab you are looking at**.

Today, asking anything about the page in front of you means leaving the browser — Telegram, the
CLI, or the Control UI — and then telling the agent, in words, which tab you meant. Two things
fall out of that:

- **No per-tab context.** Every surface shares one conversation, so a question about the tab you
  are on lands in the same thread as everything else, and the agent has to guess which of the
  shared tabs you mean.
- **The high-value cases are the annoying ones.** Filling a long form or a detailed
  questionnaire is exactly the task you want to hand to an agent *while looking at it* — and
  exactly the task that is painful to drive from a chat app on your phone.

## Why This Change Was Made

The extension already owns the hard parts — the relay, `chrome.debugger`, and the tab-group
consent model. The missing piece is a **conversation surface pinned to a tab**, so this PR adds
a side panel on top of what #100619 merged rather than building anything new underneath it:

- **Transport is unchanged.** The panel does not touch the relay. It opens its own gateway
  WebSocket as an ordinary operator client (protocol v4, Ed25519 device identity), so the relay
  stays a pure CDP/tab-consent plane and the panel is just another gateway client.
- **The tab is the conversation.** Each pinned tab gets a deterministic session key
  (`<agent-main>:thread:tab-<id>`), so two tabs never mix context and reopening the panel on a
  tab resumes its thread. The key *is* the identity — no client-side history storage.
- **Consent is reused, not re-invented.** The panel can only ask the agent to act on tabs you
  shared into the OpenClaw tab group; its "Stop sharing" button routes through the extension's
  existing `toggleShareTab` handler. Dragging a tab out (or dismissing Chrome's banner) revokes
  the agent exactly as before.
- **Least privilege.** The panel requests only `operator.read` + `operator.write`. Two
  consequences, both deliberate: "New chat" mints a fresh per-tab key generation instead of
  calling the admin-only `sessions.reset`, and tab targeting rides a message preamble rather
  than the admin-only `browser.request`. No admin scope, no new privileged surface.

**Scope boundary.** This supersedes this PR's previous node-anchored design, which stacked on
#93411 (`gateway.tools.byNode`). #100619 made that unnecessary — it proxies browser actions to a
node host natively — so #93411 is closed and all of the node-anchored routing, the
`extension-bridge` driver, and the second bridge/relay are dropped. What remains is the side
panel and per-tab sessions, layered on the merged extension. No core, gateway, or protocol
changes.

## User Impact

Open the popup, click **Open copilot panel**, and ask for things in plain language about the tab
you are on — "fill this form with my details", "summarize this thread". The agent drives that
tab through the normal `browser` tool.

- **Per-tab conversations.** Each tab keeps its own thread; **New chat** starts a fresh one.
- **Setup.** On the same machine the panel pairs silently on loopback; a remote gateway needs a
  one-time `openclaw devices` approval. Gateway URL/token live in the panel's ⚙ settings, and a
  gateway-hosted relay pairing already names the gateway, so remote setups need no second URL.
- **Nothing changes if you do not open it.** The popup, relay, tab group, and `chrome` profile
  behave exactly as they do today; the panel is additive.
- **Compatibility.** No config surface added, no defaults changed, no migration.

Docs: `docs/tools/chrome-extension.md` gains a "Side panel copilot" section.

## Evidence

**Real behavior, paired before/after, same surface, real Chromium 152** (not headless
Chrome-for-Testing). Identical scenario both sides: load the extension, pair, share the
example.org tab, open the popup from the toolbar, and use the panel to ask the agent to navigate
that shared tab to wikipedia.org.

| | Base (`c94da0df6f3`) | This PR (`a8c8f2c68ab`) |
|---|---|---|
| Popup buttons | `Stop sharing this tab`, `Unpair` | + **`Open copilot panel`** |
| `sidepanel.html` | does not exist | docks as a real side panel |
| Ask about this tab | **no surface exists** | panel pins the tab, streams the reply |
| Shared tab | stays on example.org | **driven to wikipedia.org in ~10s** |

### Visual before/after (same surface, real Chromium 152)

**Before — base `c94da0df6f3`.** Same extension popup, same clicks. Only "Stop sharing this tab"
and "Unpair": there is no copilot surface to open, so the scenario cannot start.

![Before: base popup has no copilot panel button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anagnorisis2peripeteia/openclaw/proof-93680-assets/01-before-popup-base.png)

**After — this PR.** The popup gains "Open copilot panel"; clicking it docks the side panel,
which shows green **Connected**, pins the shared tab, and reports "This tab has its own
conversation".

![After: side panel docked, Connected, pinned to the shared tab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anagnorisis2peripeteia/openclaw/proof-93680-assets/02-after-panel-docked.png)

**After — asking in natural language.** Typing the request into the panel:

![After: request typed into the side panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anagnorisis2peripeteia/openclaw/proof-93680-assets/03-after-typed.png)

**After — the agent drives the shared tab.** The panel streams the reply and two `browser` tool
steps, and the *same* tab moves example.org → wikipedia.org (note the tab is still inside the
orange **OpenClaw** tab group — the consent boundary held):

![After: panel conversation and the shared tab now on wikipedia.org](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anagnorisis2peripeteia/openclaw/proof-93680-assets/04-after-driven-wikipedia.png)

- **Before (base):** the extension exposes no copilot surface — `sidepanel.html` is absent and
  `popup.html`/`popup.js` contain zero panel references. The popup renders only "Stop sharing
  this tab" and "Unpair", so the scenario cannot proceed: there is nothing to open.
- **After (this PR):** the same popup exposes "Open copilot panel"; the panel docks, shows green
  **Connected**, pins the shared tab ("This tab has its own conversation"), and typing
  *"Navigate this tab to wikipedia.org"* + Send streamed the assistant reply plus two `browser`
  tool steps and drove the **same** tab (`E1A50B8F1A849579F7B316844119F354`) from example.org to
  `https://www.wikipedia.org/`. Independently confirmed:

```
# before the turn
1. Example Domain [use: t1 tab: t1]
   https://example.org/
   id: E1A50B8F1A849579F7B316844119F354

# after the turn (same id, no new tab)
1. Wikipedia [use: t1 tab: t1]
   https://www.wikipedia.org/
   id: E1A50B8F1A849579F7B316844119F354
```

A live-only bug this proof caught (and this PR fixes): the panel first sent an invented
`client.id`, which the gateway enums — the handshake failed with `invalid connect params: at
/client/id`. Unit tests and static checks cannot see that; only a real gateway handshake can.

**Tests / checks**

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/chrome-extension/modules/panel-core.test.ts` — 32 passing.
  Covers the per-tab key derivation (incl. the generation suffix), the protocol-v4 delta
  segmenter (incremental `deltaText`, cumulative-snapshot idempotency, `replace=true`,
  runId reset, tool-boundary segmentation, buffer-reset rebase), markdown escaping, and the
  gateway-URL derivation.
- **Mutation** (`marmorkrebs --tool stryker` on `modules/panel-core.js`): score **0.96**, 172
  mutants, 7 survivors. The survivors it first surfaced were real gaps in the test *data* —
  single-character samples could not distinguish `` `([^`]+)` `` from `` `([^`])` ``, and no case
  exercised a loopback URL ending at the host, an escaped ampersand, or a title-less tab. Those
  are now covered (14 → 7 survivors); the remainder are equivalent mutants (a scratch array whose
  seeded element is never referenced; `String(x ?? "")` fallbacks that cannot change the result).
  Scope: the pure module is the unit-tested surface, mirroring this extension's existing boundary
  (`modules/relay-core.js` has `relay-core.test.ts`; `background.js`/`popup.js` have no unit
  tests). The chrome/DOM glue (`sidepanel.js`, `device-identity.js`, `popup.js`) is covered by the
  before/after proof above rather than mocked unit tests.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/browser/chrome-extension` — clean.
- `oxfmt` clean; `node scripts/format-docs.mjs --check` clean; `docs/docs_map.md` regenerated.

**Size (this PR only)**

```
 docs/docs_map.md                                          |   1 +
 docs/tools/chrome-extension.md                            |  25 +
 extensions/browser/chrome-extension/device-identity.js    |  65 +
 extensions/browser/chrome-extension/manifest.json         |   3 +-
 extensions/browser/chrome-extension/modules/panel-core.d.ts   |  32 +
 extensions/browser/chrome-extension/modules/panel-core.js | 176 +
 extensions/browser/chrome-extension/modules/panel-core.test.ts | 245 +
 extensions/browser/chrome-extension/popup.html            |   1 +
 extensions/browser/chrome-extension/popup.js              |  12 +
 extensions/browser/chrome-extension/sidepanel.html        | 211 +
 extensions/browser/chrome-extension/sidepanel.js          | 631 +
 11 files changed, 1401 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

The extension ships unbundled, so `sidepanel.*` and `modules/panel-core.*` ride the existing
`copy-chrome-extension.mjs` static copy with no build change, and the colocated
`panel-core.test.ts` and `panel-core.d.ts` are excluded from the shipped artifact by that
script's existing filter (matching `relay-core.js` / `.d.ts` / `.test.ts`).

**Known limitation.** `chrome.sidePanel.open()` requires a real user gesture, so the panel opens
from the popup button rather than the toolbar icon directly (the action already owns the popup
for pairing).

**Review history:** every review round on this branch (autoreview + local ClawSweeper), with the complete reviews and per-finding dispositions: https://gist.github.com/871e4fb8db67e9016c570197ccb5f099

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

target.title: refactor(gateway-client): expose request dispatch boundary
target.body:
Related: #96230

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway-internal callers can observe a request result or a later `accepted` response, but cannot distinguish a failure before the request frame entered the local WebSocket transport from a failure after dispatch. That distinction is required before later restart-recovery work can make conservative retry or refund decisions without guessing from promise settlement.

This is the first independently reviewable dependency extracted from #96230. The original PR remains frozen while its behavior is split into ordered, narrower changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The protocol client is the only layer that owns the synchronous `socket.send(...)` boundary, so this adds an optional `onDispatched` observer immediately after `send` returns successfully and routes it through the existing callback-isolation helper. The package client and high-level `callGateway` wrapper forward the same observer without changing request frames, protocol versions, timeout/abort cleanup, reconnect behavior, or `onAccepted` response semantics.

The observer contract is intentionally narrow: it means the request frame was handed to the local WebSocket transport. It does not mean the Gateway/server accepted or processed the request. The request option type lives in a dedicated small module and is re-exported from the existing protocol-client module, preserving import and structural type compatibility. `GatewayClient` forwards that shared option shape as a unit, then overrides only its normalized `expectFinal` and `timeoutMs` values; this keeps the oversized implementation LOC-neutral without deleting unrelated comments.

This is a root-cause boundary fix: higher layers no longer need to infer whether transport dispatch happened. The gateway-client package is private and the new field is additive and optional. A consumer/test-double sweep covered the package export, OpenClaw facade, SDK transport, accepted-response caller, both affected request stubs, and the node-host bridge. The node-host bridge only forwards `timeoutMs` across its IPC boundary, so later recovery code must use `callGateway` or introduce a separate IPC dispatch acknowledgement rather than assuming this observer is available there.

Out of scope for this PR: Plugin SDK/session-state isolation, recovery persistence, `mainRestartRecovery` admission or ownership, bounded recovery, quarantine, and Doctor repair. In particular, this PR does not write any production recovery state.

## User Impact

There is no direct end-user behavior change. Existing callers behave exactly as before; later recovery PRs can use a precise local transport-dispatch fact instead of broad failure inference.

Risk is limited to an additive observer callback. It is not invoked when WebSocket send throws, observer exceptions are isolated from request settlement, and the callback must not be interpreted as server acceptance.

## Evidence

Focused TDD reproduction before the original implementation:


target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

### Standalone concurrent-process behavior proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.15.0, exact `@lancedb/lancedb@0.30.0`, one fresh temporary local LanceDB directory. This proof ran outside Vitest. The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

Pre-fix control: the same final-head snapshot with only `{ existOk: true }` removed while retaining the test access hook:

```text
initializer 2: failed (1)
initializer 3: failed (1)
initializer 4: failed (1)
initializer 5: failed (1)
initializer 1: failed (1)
initializer 6: ok
Error: Table memories already exists
before_exit=1
```

Final head:

```text
initializer 5: ok
initializer 1: ok
initializer 3: ok
initializer 6: ok
initializer 4: ok
initializer 2: ok
tables: memories
rows: 0
after_exit=0
```

The final table is usable, all six initializers return successfully, and the temporary schema row is removed.

### Tests and gates

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.concurrent.test.ts` under Node 24.15.0 — 2 files and 126 tests passed.
- `check:changed` passed conflict markers, the TypeScript LOC ratchet, attributions, extension export guards, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and formatting. Its repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline reports a hash mismatch; the exact baseline command reproduces the same mismatch on a clean detached `origin/main` snapshot, so this PR does not introduce it.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Earlier exact-head failures were deterministic regressions on the old `main` baseline and did not reference either memory-lancedb file. target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
